1. No, I would not perform rifampicin drug-resistance testing on this patient's initial diagnostic specimen. The Xpert MTB/RIF test has already indicated rifampicin resistance, so further testing would not provide additional useful information.

2. I would send a mycobacterial culture on this patient after the initial diagnostic specimen has been collected, as it is a standard practice to confirm the diagnosis of tuberculosis and to identify the specific strain. This is especially important in cases where the Xpert MTB/RIF test is positive but the sputum smear is negative.

3. Assuming the initial test confirms drug-susceptible pulmonary tuberculosis, I would start the patient on a 6-month treatment regimen with the following phases and dosing schedule:
(a) The treatment regimen would have two phases: an intensive phase (2 months) and a continuation phase (4 months).
(b) During the intensive phase, the patient would take isoniazid (H), rifampicin (R), pyrazinamide (Z), and ethambutol (E) daily for 2 months, with the dosing schedule being H 5 mg/kg, R 10 mg/kg, Z 15-20 mg/kg, and E 15-20 mg/kg once daily. During the continuation phase, the patient would take H and R daily for 4 months, with the dosing schedule being H 5 mg/kg and R 10 mg/kg once daily.
